brewing.notes: A safe starting point for black tea: Western style, water just off the boil.

description:
A savoury drink of tea boiled in milk with black pepper and salt, also known as Tatar tea. It is served in bowls with butter or kaymak.

This is a way of preparing tea more than a tea you buy under one name, so the recipe and the base tea change from one maker to the next.
history: It belongs with the Indian and Tibetan way of boiling tea and milk together, unlike the British habit of adding milk to strained tea. It is taken as a side dish or part of a meal, with bread and pastries dipped in it. Little more is documented about its history.
processing: Tea is boiled until strong, then one part water to two parts milk is added and brought back up; pepper and salt go in before the boil, and the mix is strained.
harvest_season: Not tied to a harvest: it depends on the base tea.
appearance_dry: Usually dark twisted leaf, sometimes with golden tips.
taste_profile: Expect what black teas usually give: malty, sweet and brisk.
vintage_note: Not sold by vintage: it is made from whatever base tea the maker keeps, so freshness of the base matters more than the year.
